artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $X = \{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$ be a finite set of unknowns. A word equation over $X$ is a pair $(u,v) \in X^* \times X^*$, usually written $u = v$. A solution of the equation $u=v$ in the free monoid $\Sigma^*$ is a morphism $h : X^* \to \Sigma^*$ such that $h(u) = h(v)$.

Two systems $S_1$ and $S_2$ of word equations over $X$ are said to be equivalent if they have exactly the same set of solutions $h : X^* \to \Sigma^*$. A subsystem of a system $S$ is any subset of the equations in $S$.

By the compactness property of free monoids (the Ehrenfeucht conjecture, proved by Albert–Lawrence and by Guba), every system $S$ of word equations over the finitely many unknowns $X$ is equivalent to some finite subsystem of itself.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $k$, depending only on the number $n$ of unknowns (and not on the system $S$), such that every system $S$ of word equations over $n$ unknowns is equivalent to one of its subsystems consisting of at most $k$ equations? Equivalently, is the maximal cardinality of an independent system of word equations on $n$ unknowns finite, and if so, can a uniform bound $k = k(n)$ be given?
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics on words / independent systems of word equations
artifact.status_search_result: The general question — whether the size of an independent system of word equations on n unknowns is bounded — is open for n ≥ 3. It is trivial for n = 2. For n = 3, an upper bound of 18 has been established (Holub and others), while constructions give independent systems of size Θ(n^4). The compactness property (Ehrenfeucht conjecture) guarantees a finite equivalent subsystem exists for each system, but no uniform bound k = k(n) is known in general.

status_evidence.title: Independent Systems of Word Equations: From Ehrenfeucht to Eighteen
status_evidence.snippet: The maximal size of an independent system of three-variable equations is at most 18.
status_evidence.claim: For n=3 unknowns, a finite upper bound (18) on the size of an independent system has been proven; the question is otherwise open.

status_evidence.title: On Maximal Chains of Systems of Word Equations
status_evidence.snippet: A big open question is whether the size of an independent system of equations over n unknowns is bounded, and this is open already for three unknowns.
status_evidence.claim: The boundedness of independent systems on n unknowns is an open problem for n ≥ 3.
